questions.q: What are the six data types JSON supports?
options: String, number, boolean, null, object, array
String, integer, float, date, object, array
Text, number, true, false, comment, function
String, number, boolean, undefined, object, array
questions.explain: JSON's entire type system is exactly six types: string, number, boolean, null, object, and array — nothing else, including no native date or function type.

questions.q: In JSON, how must object keys be written?
options: Unquoted, like plain variable names
In single quotes
Always as strings in double quotes
As numbers only
questions.explain: JSON requires every object key to be a string in double quotes — single quotes and unquoted keys are both invalid JSON.

questions.q: Why is {"id": 42,} (with a comma before the closing brace) invalid JSON?
options: Because numbers can't be values in JSON
Because JSON doesn't allow trailing commas after the last key/value pair
Because the key "id" is not a valid key name
It's actually valid JSON
questions.explain: JSON syntax forbids a trailing comma after the final item in an object or array — strict comma rules are one of the most common sources of invalid JSON.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a JSON object and a JSON array?
options: There is no difference; they're interchangeable
An object is unordered and looked up by key name; an array is ordered and looked up by position
Arrays can only contain numbers
Objects can only appear at the top level of a document
questions.explain: Objects (curly braces) are unordered key/value pairs accessed by name; arrays (square brackets) are ordered lists accessed by numeric position.

questions.q: Since JSON has no native date type, how do APIs typically represent a date or timestamp?
options: They can't — dates are impossible in JSON
As a string, in a format both sides agree on
As a special unquoted date literal
As a boolean
questions.explain: JSON has no dedicated date type, so dates travel as strings (e.g. ISO 8601) by convention — a common source of pitfalls covered in Lesson 10.
